context.exploration_scope: Independently validated the application boundary of PHASE-SSI-S19's confirmed capability Principle against the real Goal/Capability landscape beyond cap_dataset_management, deliberately including goal_production_runtime as a surface-similar-but-different-real-cause trap case

problem: PHASE-SSI-S19 confirmed the capability Principle works correctly on its own evidenced case (goal_semantic_quality), but a Principle checked only against the case it came from hasn't demonstrated it knows its own boundary -- specifically whether it would misfire on goal_production_runtime, which shares the same surface shape (blocked, tied to a capability) but has a completely unrelated real cause.

decision.decision_summary: Boundary rule (mechanical, grounded in trace v16's own capability_status_clarification field): applies only when that field is present and non-empty. Tested against all 3 real chains: goal_semantic_quality(applies=true,expected=true,correct=true), goal_production_runtime(applies=false,expected=false,correct=true), goal_ghibli_production_pipeline(applies=false,expected=false,correct=true). All correct: true. Duplication/conflict against E12/S4: false. Verdict: PRINCIPLE_BOUNDARY_VALIDATED.

action.action_summary: Re-checked duplication/conflict against E12's confirmed Pattern registry and the S4 Principle; stated the application/non-application boundary as a mechanical rule grounded in trace v16's own structure; tested that rule against all 3 real chains, including goal_production_runtime as a deliberate surface-similar trap case.

result.note: The boundary rule correctly applied to goal_semantic_quality and correctly refused goal_production_runtime (the surface-similar trap case) and goal_ghibli_production_pipeline -- the capability Principle's boundary is real, not just untested.

cause.root_cause_summary: goal_production_runtime and goal_semantic_quality share an identical surface shape (blocked, tied to a named capability) while differing completely on real cause (external infrastructure vs internal entity-concentration misattribution) -- exactly the kind of pair that would fool a boundary rule based on surface status alone, which is why it was deliberately included rather than testing only cases already known to be safe.

lesson: Validating a second Principle's boundary means deliberately hunting for the surface-similar trap case, not just re-confirming cases already known to pass -- goal_production_runtime looked exactly like a case this Principle might wrongly claim, and the mechanical, structure-grounded rule (capability_status_clarification presence, not "blocked" status) correctly refused it.
